questions.question: A stakeholder asks for a "magical" new AI feature that hasn't been tested. Your first move is:

answers.text: Build a quick Streamlit UI with a mocked backend to see if the value is there.
Map out the data pipelines and API schema required to make it production-ready.
Evaluate the potential token costs and latency impact against existing SLAs.

questions.question: When choosing between a complex Agentic workflow and a simple RAG setup for a standard query task, you prioritize:

answers.text: The Agentic workflow—it's more flexible for discovering edge cases.
The RAG setup—it's easier to integrate into the current application stack.
The RAG setup—it offers more predictable costs and lower hallucination risks.

questions.question: Your preferred development environment for a new AI project is:

answers.text: A Jupyter Notebook or Google Colab for rapid iteration and visualization.
A local IDE with a robust CI/CD pipeline and containerization.
A managed platform with built-in experiment tracking and drift monitoring.

questions.question: What does "Technical Taste" mean to you in an AI context?

answers.text: Sensing which experimental ideas will actually move the needle for the user.
Choosing the right architecture to ensure the system doesn't break at launch.
Balancing performance, cost, and risk to maintain a sustainable system.

questions.question: You discover a high hallucination rate in a prototype. You solve it by:

answers.text: Prompt engineering and trying three different alternative models immediately.
Refining the data chunking strategy and improving the retrieval metadata.
Implementing a secondary "Guardrail" LLM to validate all outputs before they reach the user.

questions.question: Which metric is most important for a successful AI deployment?

answers.text: Time to Value (how fast we proved the concept).
System uptime and API response reliability.
Cost-per-query vs. business ROI.

questions.question: Regarding data privacy and PII (Personally Identifiable Information):

answers.text: It's a hurdle to be addressed once the core value proposition is proven.
It's a requirement handled through secure data pipelines and access controls.
It's a primary constraint that determines which models and regions we are allowed to use.

questions.question: The project is falling behind schedule. To catch up, you would:

answers.text: Reduce the scope to a "lo-fi" version to get it in front of users faster.
Automate the testing suite to find and fix architectural bugs more quickly.
Optimize the most expensive/slowest model calls to improve immediate performance.

questions.question: Your team is debating a move to a new open-source model. You argue based on:

answers.text: The potential for higher "vibe" quality and creative output.
The ease of self-hosting and integration into existing Kubernetes clusters.
The long-term reduction in vendor lock-in and inference costs.

questions.question: A "Builder" archetype is most valuable when:

answers.text: A company is in the "zero to one" phase of product discovery.
A validated idea needs to be turned into a scalable, end-to-end production system.
A system is already live but suffers from high latency and governance gaps.
I re-run my best prompts to see if the "vibe" still feels right.
I update the underlying data index and re-verify the integration points.
I set up automated observability alerts and a versioned model fallback strategy.

questions.question: In terms of seniority, when working under high ambiguity, you:

answers.text: Iterate faster to "fail forward" and find clarity through action.
Design modular systems that can be easily refactored as requirements change.
Establish a rigorous governance framework to mitigate risks while the path is unclear.
